title: Dedicated tenant guardrails and adaptive bursting (PRD)
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Overview: This PRD defines a set of tenant-level guardrails and an adaptive bursting mechanism for Redwood Dedicated. The goal is to allow tenants to safely exceed baseline reserved capacity for short windows (burst), while protecting co-tenants and preserving latency SLOs. We propose a burst reservoir model combined with SLO-aware throttling, soft-preemption, and transparent telemetry for tenants and ops.

Problem statement: Customers want predictable baseline throughput from Reserved Pools but also need occasional short-lived spikes without painful manual capacity commits. Current behaviors either deny bursts (rigid isolation) or allow bursts that destabilize other tenants. We need an operationally safe way to offer controlled elasticity that is transparent and enforceable across zones and hardware classes.

User personas: 
- Platform SRE (operator): needs deterministic overload behavior, audit trails, and simple rollback knobs.
- Tenant infra engineer: wants burst headroom for traffic spikes, predictable cost, and controls over how and when bursting occurs.
- Product manager / feature owner: wants SLA-preserving fallbacks and metrics to justify capacity purchases.

High-level proposal: Implement a Guardrail + Reservoir system: each reserved pool exposes a configurable "burst reservoir" (time-windowed credit bank) and a set of guardrails (max sustained rate, preemption class, warmup policy). Runtime enforces admission using SLO-aware scoring (latency headroom, KV-cache occupancy) and a priority-backed fallback chain. Operators can set global emergency thresholds and tenants can opt into burst budgets with configurable RTO and cost attribution.
goals: Allow short bursts up to configurable budget without violating cluster latency SLOs
Provide transparent accounting and billing attribution for burst usage
Give operators deterministic preemption paths and telemetry for post-incident analysis
Ship with a minimal UI surface in Console for tenants to view/adjust burst budgets and see historical usage
non_goals: Replace existing long-term reservation pricing model
Auto-scale baseline reserved capacity without explicit commit or contract
Fully autonomous model selection or re-compilation optimizations (out of scope for initial rollout)
success_metrics: Fraction of burst events that complete within tenant SLO without ops intervention >= 85% (first 90 days)
Reduction in emergency capacity escalations attributed to spikes by 60% q/q
No measurable degradation (p99 latency) for protected tenants during bursts; nightly checks <= 5% regressions
Billing: X% of tenants adopt optional burst budgets within 2 quarters (adoption target: 20%)
requirements_functional: Per-tenant burst reservoir: configurable capacity (credits), recharge window, and max single-event drawdown
Guardrail policies: max sustained QPS, preemption class (soft/hard), and fallback chain to smaller models or hosted routing
Admission controller evaluates incoming requests against: current reservoir balance, target latency headroom, and cache/KV occupancy; returns allow/queue/deny
Transparent accounting: per-request burst flag, credit delta, and cost tag propagated to billing and Console telemetry
Operator emergency throttle: cluster-level kill-switch and fast rollback for reservoir parameters
UI: Console panel showing reservoir balance, usage timeline, predicted exhaustion time, and a one-click revoke
APIs: Tenant-facing endpoints to query reservoir state and to subscribe to webhook alerts when thresholds cross
Fallbacks: automatic model variant fallback when reservoir exhausted, following tenant-configured priority order
Observability: new dashboards (per-tenant) for burst events, preemption incidents, and impact on latency/cost
Audit logs: immutable records for reservoir configuration changes and manual overrides
requirements_nonfunctional: Admission decision latency budget: additional wall-clock decision time <= 2ms p95
Reservoir accounting accuracy: credit reconciliation drift <= 0.1% per 24h
Runtime isolation: enforcement hooks must be compatible with dedicated autoscaler and not block normal scheduling
Security: reservoir APIs respect tenant RBAC and KMS keys for audit exports
Scalability: support 10k active reservoirs in a single region without >10% increase in scheduling latency
Backward compatibility: tenants without reservoir config must experience current behavior (no silent changes)
acceptance_criteria: E2E test: synthetic tenant simulating spike workload uses burst credits and completes at expected latency; test must run in staging and pass for 3 consecutive runs
Observability: Console shows per-tenant burst usage graph and raw logs are queryable in central logging within 60s
Billing: burst-tagged requests are reflected in billing pipeline with correct cost attribution in test account
Preemption path: when reservoir exhausted, requests are either queued or fall back per tenant priority; documented test demonstrates fallback triggers
Operator controls: emergency revoke and rollback perform within 30s and an audit entry is logged
Performance: admission decision latency median <1ms and p95 <2ms under staging load profile
scope_changes_considered: Initially considered per-tenant machine-level hot prewarm (node-specific reservation) but pushed to future scope due to complexity in scheduler integration. Also evaluated fully automatic baseline autoscaling; deferred pending contractual and billing model changes.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (staging): implement reservoir accounting, admission controller, and basic fallback chain (model variant only). Phase 2 (pilot): onboard 3 enterprise tenants with opt-in console controls and close collaboration with SRE. Phase 3 (gradual rollout): region-by-region enablement behind operator flags, auto-telemetry checks, and documentation. Final step: public GA with pricing and billing flow. Expected timeline: 8 weeks engineering + 3 weeks pilot + 2 weeks ramp to GA readiness.
risks_mitigations: Risk: Reservoir mis-accounting could lead to unfair tenant chargebacks. Mitigation: reconcile batch job with alerts and manual correction path; require two-phase commit for config changes.

Risk: Poorly-configured guardrails causing noisy neighbor events. Mitigation: default conservative reservoir sizes and allow tenants to request increased budgets via contacts; use simulation runs before changing production knobs.
Risk: Admission controller becoming hot path (latency). Mitigation: micro-optimized evaluation, use cached reservoir snapshots, and fall back to deny-on-timeout policy to protect SLOs.
dependencies: ENG-1842 (runtime admission hooks and KV cache occupancy metrics)
ENG-2301 (billing pipeline: tag propagation and cost attribution)
ENG-2999 (console: new panel and webhook service)

decisions: MVP will support single-zone reservoirs only to simplify enforcement and avoid cross-zone coordination complexity
Reservoir accounting will be eventually consistent with strong reconciliation process; runtime uses snapshot reads for admission decisions
Default pilot reservoir config will be conservative: 5-minute window equivalent of 2x baseline throughput with max single drawdown capped at 50% of reservoir
open_questions: Should tenants be allowed to purchase burst credits proactively (pre-bought bucket) or only consume on-demand with billed overage?
How will cross-region failover interact with reservoir semantics for multi-region dedicated customers?
What SLAs (if any) do we offer for burst completion vs baseline reservation?
